page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a compute- and memory-focused virtual machine configured with constrained core sizing to optimize per-core software licensing costs. Driven by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance runs on a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture at clock speeds reaching 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources consist of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. Integrated instruction sets include AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 matrix acceleration extensions.

The hardware configuration features 336.0 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 84.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture incorporates a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD, supporting direct high-speed transient input/output operations alongside Azure Premium Storage compatibility. The server contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators, relying exclusively on CPU execution units for compute tasks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution driven by the 4.2 GHz Intel core frequency. In Geekbench testing, single-core execution reached top-tier performance with a score of 2357.0, corroborated by strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.85 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core throughput is bounded by the 4-vCPU ceiling, recording lower-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng workloads at 4437.16 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 28.27 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth measured 345.84 GB/sec for small cached blocks, tapering to 36.33 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads.

This server architecture presents a deliberate hardware tradeoff designed for high-memory, licensing-constrained workloads rather than parallel compute scalability. The extreme ratio of 336.0 GB RAM to 4 vCPUs makes it well aligned for relational database management systems, in-memory caches such as Redis, Electronic Design Automation, and high-frequency analytical batch processing requiring substantial memory capacity per CPU core.
